questions.subject: BIOLOGY
options: is a repeat of the original experiment to make sure results are reproducible
is carried out at a constant temperature
is always carried out under the controlled conditions of a laboratory
helps interpret the results of the main experiment
is simpler than a real experiment
explanation_steps: A control isolates the variable under test so results of the main experiment can be interpreted.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Adaptation is the process by which
options: new varieties of plants are selected for use in agriculture
organisms become better suited to their environment
individuals of one species interact with individuals of another species
a lethal reaction occurs in response to an unusual stimulus
non-biological predators leave for a while
explanation_steps: Adaptation is becoming better suited to the environment.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT true of cells?
options: The cell is the structural unit of life
The cell is the unit of function of living things
Cells come from pre-existing cells
The molecules of life are products of cell activity
Cells are surrounded by a cell wall
explanation_steps: Animal cells have a plasma membrane but no cell wall. Cell walls are not universal.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
options: do not have different types of cells with specialised functions.
have organs, but not tissues.
have only one tissue.
have tissues, but no organs.
have only one organ.
explanation_steps: Sponges have specialized cell types forming tissue-level organization but lack true organs.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: According to the modern classification of organisms, humans are members of:
options: the chordate phylum.
the vertebrate order.
the primate class.
the Homoidae order.
The Homo species.
explanation_steps: Humans belong to Phylum Chordata. Vertebrata is a subphylum, Primates is an order, Homo is a genus, Hominidae is a family.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
options: are commonly found in deserts.
occur in most permanent or semi-permanent bodies of water.
have specialised tissues for conducting water and food.
reproduce only asexually.
are usually heterotrophic.
explanation_steps: Algae are aquatic photosynthetic organisms found in permanent and semi-permanent water bodies. They lack vascular tissue and are autotrophic.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
options: refer to several kinds of fungi that form mycelium.
contain chlorophyll.
are major parasites of crop plants, particularly the cereals.
are used in the process of industrial fermentation.
belong to the class Deuteromycetes.
explanation_steps: Yeasts are unicellular fungi used in industrial fermentation (bread, alcohol). They do not contain chlorophyll.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Bryophytes differ from pteridophytes in that bryophytes:
options: contain chlorophyll.
show an alternation of generations.
reproduce sexually.
have rhizomes.
lack specialised tissues for conducting water and food.
explanation_steps: Bryophytes are non-vascular; pteridophytes have xylem and phloem.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Monocots and dicots are the same in their:
options: cotyledon number.
leaf venation pattern.
capacity to produce seeds.
vascular bundle arrangement.
root system.
explanation_steps: Both are seed-producing angiosperms. They differ in cotyledon number, venation, vascular arrangement and roots.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: An example of nastic movement in plants is:
options: roots grow down, while shoots grow up.
the closing of a flower in the evening.
branches bending in the wind.
plant growth towards sunlight.
root growth towards water or nutrients.
explanation_steps: Nastic movements are non-directional responses (e.g. nyctinasty: flowers closing at night). Tropisms are directional.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
options: the transportation of water from roots to leaves.
the evaporation of water from above-ground parts of a plant.
the exchange of gases that takes place at the surface of a leaf.
the absorption of water through non-root parts of the plant.
the transport of nutrients through the vascular system of a plant.
explanation_steps: Transpiration is loss of water vapour from aerial parts, mainly leaves.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
options: the species survives.
children are genetically different from their parents.
each new body cell has the same genetic make-up as its parent cell.
gametes are produced for the next generation.
the chromosome number is halved.
explanation_steps: Mitosis produces genetically identical body cells. Meiosis halves chromosome number and produces gametes.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: In the second division of meiosis:
options: chromatids separate.
the chromosome number is halved.
homologous chromosomes come together.
homologous chromosomes separate.
chromatids stay together.
explanation_steps: Meiosis I separates homologues and halves the number. Meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
options: two parents are required to produce each offspring.
the offspring result from conjugation.
the offspring are genetically different from the parents.
an unfertilised egg develops into an embryo.
a single-celled organism divides into two equal daughter cells.
explanation_steps: Parthenogenesis is development of an embryo from an unfertilised egg.
